verbalization: The visible evidence suggests that stiripentol may interact with Selenoprotein P through multiple indirect pathways. The drug is reported to target several unrelated proteins, including Far upstream element-binding protein 1, Keratin, type II cytoskeletal 1, and Complement factor B. These proteins are each targeted by other molecules, including Leronlimab, Influenza B virus hemagglutinin, and Selgantolimod, respectively. All of these molecules ultimately have Selenoprotein P as their target. This indicates that stiripentol may exert its effects through a network of molecular interactions that ultimately converge on Selenoprotein P. The evidence is consistent with a mechanism where stiripentol influences downstream targets that, in turn, affect Selenoprotein P. The strength of the evidence is moderate, as the relationships are indirect and involve multiple layers of molecular interactions. The exact nature of the interaction between stiripentol and Selenoprotein P remains uncertain, and further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the direct relationship.
